zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 3; they partially obstruct ocean view cabins on Deck 2 (worst affected), Deck 3 (boats at cabin level), and lower Deck 6 cabins (minimal obstruction, horizon clear).
zones.effect: On Deck 2, you look directly at boat davits and hulls with limited ocean visible; Deck 3 views are interrupted by boat structures; Deck 6 loses some downward view but keeps clear horizon.
zones.mattersTo: Critical for anyone choosing an ocean view cabin on Deck 2 who expects open sea views; less important on Deck 3; mostly irrelevant on Deck 6 where the horizon remains unobstructed and veranda cabins look outward.

zones.what: The Lido Deck pool area, buffet, and outdoor activity zones sit directly above Deck 10 forward and extend over portions of Deck 9.
zones.effect: Expect deck chair dragging, pool activity, and foot traffic overhead from early morning through late evening; most pronounced on Deck 10 directly beneath the main pool deck.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone sensitive to overhead noise should avoid Deck 10 entirely; matters less to those spending days ashore or who sleep through ambient noise.

zones.what: Deck 11 aft sits directly below the Sunrise Deck (Deck 12) open-air jogging track and sports court.
zones.effect: Jogging track overhead means rhythmic footfalls from early morning joggers; sports court adds ball bouncing and activity noise during the day.
zones.mattersTo: Early risers bothered by footsteps overhead should choose elsewhere; non-issue for those who rise late or don't mind ambient outdoor activity sounds.

zones.what: The Celebrity Theater (main showroom) occupies Decks 4 and 5 forward, two to three decks below forward cabins on Decks 7 and 8.
zones.effect: Late-night shows (typically ending 10:30-11pm) may produce bass vibration or muffled sound transmission upward, though separation of two-plus decks significantly dampens this.
zones.mattersTo: Very sensitive sleepers going to bed before 11pm might notice; most guests find the distance sufficient insulation, especially with modern soundproofing.

zones.what: The two-deck Continuum restaurant and indoor/outdoor spaces occupy Decks 4-5 aft, directly below aft cabins on Decks 6 and 7.
zones.effect: Dining service noise, kitchen activity, and guest traffic during meal hours; most intense during breakfast and dinner service.
zones.mattersTo: Those in aft cabins on Decks 6-7 wanting quiet during mealtimes should be aware; typically subsides after dinner service ends.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks are located forward and amidships on all cabin decks, with forward banks serving all decks and midship banks serving Decks 2-11.
zones.effect: Cabins immediately adjacent to elevator lobbies have convenient access but experience intermittent door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic at all hours; cabins one or two away get convenience without most noise.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests prioritize proximity; light sleepers should choose cabins at least two doors away from the elevator vestibule.

zones.what: Engine room machinery sits below and slightly aft of the lowest cabin decks; aft cabins on Decks 2 and 3 are closest to propulsion systems.
zones.effect: Potential for low-frequency vibration underway, most noticeable during maneuvering or high-speed sailing; typically steady and many find it becomes background white noise.
zones.mattersTo: Those highly sensitive to vibration should choose mid or forward sections; others often find it unnoticeable or even soothing.

zones.what: Bow thrusters operate in the forward section below the lowest cabin decks, used during docking and maneuvering in port.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical grinding or rumbling during port arrivals and departures, typically 15-30 minutes per event; silent during open-sea sailing.
zones.mattersTo: Only matters if you're in the cabin during port arrival/departure and are noise-sensitive; irrelevant if you're on deck or ashore during these times.

zones.what: Anchor chain locker is located in the bow below forward cabins; anchor deployment creates loud chain noise early morning in port.
zones.effect: Rattling metallic chain noise during anchoring operations, typically pre-dawn on tender port days; lasts 2-5 minutes but very audible.
zones.mattersTo: Forward cabin guests on tender port itineraries will hear this if anchoring; non-issue on all-dock itineraries or for those unbothered by brief early wake-up.

zones.what: Crew corridors (I-95) run through lower decks with access points near forward and aft stairwells; service staff use these routes for cabin service, meal delivery, and housekeeping throughout the day.
zones.effect: Cabins near crew access doors may experience brief periods of service cart traffic and crew conversation, most active during morning turndown (8-10am) and evening turndown (6-8pm).
zones.mattersTo: Guests in cabin during peak service hours may notice; those on tours or at dinner miss the activity entirely.
